title: EV charging network
brief: Thousands of chargers report their status every few seconds and send a record when a session ends. Drivers open an app to find a free charger. A session record must never be lost or counted twice, because it becomes a bill.

clarify.q: Must the status on the map be exact?
clarify.a: No. Ten seconds behind is fine. Drivers just need to know a charger is probably free.

clarify.q: Can a charger retry a session record?
clarify.a: Yes, and it will after any bad connection. A retry must not bill the driver twice.
Yes. A bill can be settled in the background, as long as no record is lost.

notes: About 20,000 chargers, each sending a status every 10 to 20 seconds (approx.).
A session record is about 1 KB (approx.).

numbers.label: Status messages per second at peak
Session records a day
numbers.how: 2 million drivers a month ÷ 30 × about 2 sessions each ≈ 130,000 (approx.)

hints: A charger will retry after a bad connection. What stops a retry from billing twice?
Put a queue between the servers and the billing work, so a slow bill never blocks a charger. Add an idempotency store so a repeated record counts once.
Load balancer, servers, idempotency store, queue and workers for sessions, a key-value store for charger status, a SQL database for sessions.

editorial.summary: Two kinds of message with two promises. Status is frequent and may be a little old, so a key-value store holds the latest. A session record must land exactly once, so it carries a unique key, goes through a queue and is stored in SQL.

designs.name: Status in a key-value store, sessions through a queue
designs.why: Chargers write only their latest status into a key-value store, which the map reads. Session records pass an idempotency store, wait in a queue and are written by workers, so retries and slow billing never lose or double a record.

tradeoffs: Keeping only the latest status per charger makes writes cheap. History, if wanted, goes to a separate cheaper store.
The idempotency store costs a lookup per record, and it is what makes retries safe.
The queue absorbs a morning rush of reconnecting chargers. Billing may lag a few minutes, which is fine.
If the billing partner is down, records wait in the queue instead of failing.
editorial.realWorld: A national charger network has tens of thousands of chargers, each sending a status every few seconds, so a thousand or more small messages a second. Session records are far fewer but must never be lost (approx.).

correctness.prompt: The same request is delivered twice, and a worker can crash after saving it. What uniqueness constraint and transaction would keep one durable result?
correctness.discussion: Choose a stable business operation id and enforce a unique constraint in the authoritative store. Insert the id, apply the change and save its result in one transaction. A retry returns that result. Recording the id before the change can lose work after a crash; recording it afterwards can apply the change twice. If work continues through a queue, commit an outbox entry in the same transaction and deduplicate at each consumer.
